headline: Warm, dry weather through Friday with possible morning fog, then cooler, unsettled weather with light rain Saturday and early next week.
summary: High pressure is building over the Northwest, and skies are clearing. Highs should reach the upper 60s to low 70s Thursday and the mid 70s Friday. Forecasters note some Minor HeatRisk both days, meaning the warmth could affect a small number of people especially sensitive to heat. Because the lower atmosphere is moist and winds are light, low cloud and possibly fog could form Thursday morning, though fog is only a possibility. Winds will blow from the east, off the land, and get a little breezy in the Cascades and foothills Thursday night, with gusts of 25 to 30 mph. Humidity could drop to around 35 to 40% in the Cascades and southern Olympics Thursday, and to 35 to 45% more widely Friday. The high pressure weakens over the weekend as a series of weak systems move through. Saturday will likely bring rain during the day, mostly to the North Cascades, with only a few hundredths of an inch in the lowlands, and parts of the Seattle area may stay dry. Highs drop to the low 60s Saturday, a sharp fall from Friday's mid 70s. Sunday looks cooler and drier, with morning lows in the low 40s around Puget Sound and mid 30s in the Cascade foothills. Cool, unsettled weather continues into early next week with more chances for light rain, especially Tuesday. Forecasters will watch the track of the offshore trough (a dip in the jet stream) for changes, and they say the pattern after Tuesday is unclear because the models disagree. Seas on the coastal waters will build over the weekend.
changes: Earlier discussions described a wetter, showery Saturday and a possible Sunday-Monday system, but by afternoon and evening Saturday looked mostly light rain, with parts of Seattle possibly dry, and Sunday cooler and drier. Forecasters also added the Minor HeatRisk, breezy east winds and lower humidity for Thursday and Friday.
